title: Police gun down man before my eyes ; Shots ring out by Tim Hortons in 'sleepy town': [Ontario Edition]
article: Star correspondent Roberta Avery walked out of a Tim Hortons in Bradford just in time to see police shoot Mark Norman Graham.
Here is her account.
"Stop, get down on the ground!" the police officer shouted.
Directly in the line of fire, 20 to 25 metres away, I froze, but the man in camouflage pants and a dark jacket kept casually walking.
The officer repeated his command three more times.

Still, the man kept walking away, almost as if he didn't believe the officer. Then he slowly reached for his bag and started to turn around. Three shots rang out in rapid succession echoing across the Barrie St. Tim Hortons parking lot.
The man spun around and fell to the ground, fatally wounded.
Horrified, I saw blood start to ooze from his upper chest area, staining the tarmac.
The three South Simcoe police officers stood momentarily rooted to the spot.
Smoke was still coming from a rifle one was holding. The other two had their pistols drawn.
Then screams, moans, shouts and sobs filled the air as shocked witnesses realized what they had just seen.
The young female officer, her hair tied in a ponytail, went over and grabbed at the man lying on his back as a male officer pointed his pistol at him.
She seized the man's left arm. It was, I noticed, covered in tattoos. And splattered with blood.
The man matched the description of a suspect wanted in an earlier shooting.
She pulled him over and away from the bag he'd been carrying on his shoulder, which was now lying partly under him.
Soon the man's head was in a pool of blood. About three metres away, what appeared to be a sawed-off shotgun was on the ground.
Within minutes, two paramedics arrived and began giving the man cardiopulmonary resuscitation. He didn't appear to respond.
Another ambulance arrived and a paramedic covered the blood on the tarmac with a white towel. It was soon stained red.
The special investigations unit, which examines all deaths and serious injuries involving police, is investigating the shooting which happened just after 2:30 p.m. yesterday.
"I couldn't believe it. Three pops and it was done and we were all there. We could have been killed; there were people everywhere," said Jake Lonsdale, 17, of Bradford, who saw the whole thing.
"The man didn't seem too worried. He just said 'I'll be back, guys,' and they started firing."
The saga started about 13 hours before, when a 39-year-old man was shot and seriously wounded outside the Trophy Case tavern about two blocks west of the Tim Hortons.
South Simcoe police believe the victim in the tavern shooting, who was fighting for his life in a Newmarket hospital late last night, knew his assailant.
Police refused to release the man's name but witnesses said he is Raymond Taillefer, who does odd jobs around town and sometimes plays guitar at Tic Tac's bar next door to the Trophy Case.
Police using tracker dogs initiated a huge search of the area for a suspect they warned was "armed and dangerous and in possession of a gun."
They identified the man they were looking for as Mark Norman Graham, 38, of no fixed address.
He was described as having tattoos of a hatchet on his right cheekbone, one of teardrops under his left eye and numerous other tattoos on his arms.
Jake Lonsdale, 17, of Bradford said he knew Graham well and he was the man police shot.
"I couldn't believe it. Three pops and it was done and we were all there. We could have been killed; there were people everywhere," said Lonsdale, 17, of Bradford, who saw the whole thing.
The owner of Tic Tac's was playing cards with several of his customers around 1 a.m. yesterday when he heard a single shot fired.
He looked out of the window to see Taillefer being carried on a stretcher to an ambulance.
"He's a good man. He does a lot of work for me," he said.
He also knew Graham and said he was scared of him.
"Don't use my name. He may come looking for me," he said.
By early yesterday afternoon, there was no sign of police activity in Bradford but the main topic of conversation was the events that had unfolded in the early hours of the morning.
"I've lived here for 16 years, and this is a quiet, sleepy town. Nothing happens," said the owner of Tic Tac's.
Shelley Wright, 36, of Lefroy arrived in Bradford yesterday afternoon to visit a friend who lives in an apartment above the Trophy Case.
"He (her friend) wasn't home and I was coming down the steps and I saw a police officer and he was yelling 'Stop! Get down on the ground,' so I hit the floor," she said.
She saw a man walking as "if he was going for a stroll.
"He was not doing anything the police said."
A group of teenagers, who were walking behind the police officers as they tailed the strolling man with their weapons drawn, were shouting abuse.
"They were egging him on not to do what the police were asking. They were telling him that the police couldn't shoot him because that's the law in Canada," said Wright.
Wright followed at a distance and heard the strolling man say, "I'm going to Newmarket for a coffee and I'll talk to you when I get back," she said.
"Then I heard three bangs and I came round the corner to see the man lying on the ground," she said.
